subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Central nervous system tumours: WHO classification, molecular diagnostics, maximal resection, chemoradiotherapy and recurrence therapy

steps.tx: The revised **WHO CNS5 classification** establishes that glioblastoma is molecularly defined by IDH-wildtype status in an infiltrative astrocytic glioma. Even in histologically lower-grade tumours lacking microvascular proliferation or necrosis, detecting TERT promoter mutations, EGFR gene amplification, or combined **chromosome 7 gain and 10 loss** is sufficient to definitively diagnose glioblastoma, WHO grade 4.

steps.tx: Epigenetic hypermethylation of the **MGMT promoter** silences transcription of the DNA repair enzyme O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase. Silencing MGMT prevents enzymatic removal of alkyl groups added by temozolomide, sensitizing tumour cells to cytotoxic replication arrest and apoptosis. In glioblastoma, MGMT promoter methylation serves as the strongest predictive biomarker for prolonged progression-free and overall survival following alkylating chemotherapy.

left.title: MGMT Methylated Promoter
points: Epigenetic silencing of MGMT DNA repair enzyme
Predicts marked survival benefit from adjuvant TMZ

right.title: MGMT Unmethylated Promoter
points: Active expression of MGMT repair protein
Rapid enzymatic removal of O6-methylguanine adducts

steps.tx: The landmark **Stupp protocol** established the universal standard of care for newly diagnosed glioblastoma. Following maximal safe surgical resection, patients receive focal radiotherapy delivering 60 Gy in 30 fractions with concurrent daily **temozolomide** at 75 mg/m2 throughout radiation, followed by 6 cycles of adjuvant maintenance temozolomide at 150 to 200 mg/m2 daily for 5 days every 28 days.

steps.tx: In the randomized phase III **EF-14 trial**, adding **Tumour treating fields** TTFields to maintenance temozolomide significantly prolonged both progression-free survival and overall survival in glioblastoma. Delivering low-intensity, intermediate-frequency 200 kHz alternating electrical fields through non-invasive ceramic transducer arrays applied to the shaved scalp disrupts mitotic spindle microtubule assembly, arresting dividing glioma cells in metaphase.

steps.tx: Adult diffuse **oligodendrogliomas** are strictly defined by co-occurrence of an IDH1 or IDH2 mutation and complete, unbalanced whole-arm **1p and 19q co-deletion**. This unique molecular profile confers marked chemosensitivity and favourable long-term prognosis. In RTOG 9402 and EORTC 26951, adding adjuvant **PCV chemotherapy** procarbazine, lomustine, and vincristine to radiotherapy dramatically doubled median overall survival beyond 14 years.

steps.tx: Oral dual mutant IDH1 and IDH2 inhibitor **Vorasidenib** was engineered specifically for high blood-brain barrier penetration. In the landmark phase III **INDIGO trial**, vorasidenib significantly prolonged progression-free survival and delayed time to next intervention in patients with residual or recurrent grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma. Vorasidenib establishes an effective targeted strategy that delays toxic radiation and chemotherapy in young adults.

steps.tx: **Medulloblastoma** is divided into 4 **molecular subgroups**: WNT associated with CTNNB1 mutations, SHH, Group 3 with MYC amplification, and Group 4. The WNT subgroup, defined by somatic CTNNB1 mutations or germline APC variants, carries an outstanding long-term prognosis with over 95% survival. Conversely, Group 3 tumours frequently harbour MYC amplification, exhibiting high rates of early leptomeningeal dissemination and poor overall survival.

steps.tx: **Medulloblastoma** is the most common malignant **posterior fossa tumour** in children and arises in the **cerebellum**. It often causes **raised intracranial pressure** and can seed through **cerebrospinal fluid**, so whole spine **MRI** is required at staging. Under **WHO CNS5**, it is classified by **molecular subgroup** (WNT, SHH, group 3 and group 4) rather than histology alone.

steps.tx: Primary CNS lymphoma is predominantly diffuse large B-cell lymphoma confined to the brain, leptomeninges, or vitreoretinal space. High-dose **methotrexate-based induction** regimens such as the **MATRix protocol** combining methotrexate, cytarabine, thiotepa, and rituximab achieve high complete remission rates. Consolidating remission with high-dose busulfan-thiotepa chemotherapy followed by autologous stem cell transplantation provides durable curative disease control without whole-brain radiation neurotoxicity.
